stories.headline: First Trump-Xi-Putin summit ends with joint pledge on nuclear-risk talks, more oil supply, UN reform

key_facts.fact: Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump held the first-ever trilateral meeting of US, Chinese and Russian leaders in Shenzhen on Thursday, November 19, 2026; the talks began around 08:30 GMT and ended around 09:50 GMT.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin held their first-ever trilateral talks Thursday in Shenzhen... The gathering ended roughly 80 minutes later at 5.50 pm local time (0950GMT), after beginning around 4.30 pm (0830GMT).

key_facts.fact: The 'China-Russia-U.S. Heads of State Declaration toward Peace' has four points: reforming the UN, increasing production and supply of refined petroleum products, warning the International Criminal Court and similar bodies against abusing their jurisdiction, and a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing proliferation.
key_facts.excerpt: The three countries plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations... the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction... The three countries will conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons.

key_facts.fact: The declaration restates that 'a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought'; Trump said the three countries were 'uniquely positioned' to discuss reducing nuclear arsenals, while China has repeatedly refused to join disarmament talks, citing its estimated 620 warheads vs. 5,042 for the US and 5,420 for Russia (SIPRI).
key_facts.excerpt: Trump said Washington, Moscow and Beijing were "uniquely positioned" to discuss reducing nuclear arsenals... China possessed an estimated 620 nuclear warheads as of January 2026, compared with 5,042 held by the US and 5,420 by Russia.

key_facts.fact: Trump's one-on-one with Putin lasted 42 minutes and his talks with Xi about an hour; a Kremlin aide said Ukraine was the focus of the Putin meeting and that Putin left 'in an excellent mood'.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump's meeting with Putin lasted 42 minutes. His talks with Xi went about an hour... a Kremlin aide would only say that Ukraine had been the focus of the discussions — adding the Kremlin leader had left "in an excellent mood."

key_facts.fact: Trump declined to answer journalists' questions about China's alleged role in an espionage plot to obtain high-end Nvidia chips.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump refused to engage with journalists' questions over China's alleged role in an espionage plot to steal high end Nvidia chips.

key_facts.fact: The separate APEC leaders' statement, titled the 'Shenzhen Outlook', makes no mention of the WTO or of rare earths, a key point of US-China tension.
key_facts.excerpt: The one produced in Shenzhen, however, is called the "Shenzhen Outlook."... it has no mention of the World Trade Organization or support for the multilateral trading system... It does not mention rare earths -- a key point of tension between the U.S. and China.

key_facts.fact: On the eve of the summit, Zelensky told NBC News that if China and the US imposed or threatened sanctions on Russia, 'that's the end of the war'.
key_facts.excerpt: If China and the United States imposed or threatened sanctions on Russia, "that's the end of the war," Zelenskyy told NBC News in an exclusive interview.

stories.headline: Trump weighs new Iran strikes as Netanyahu pushes a 4-to-7-day joint air campaign; Gulf states lobby against

key_facts.fact: The New York Times reported Wednesday that Trump is weighing another round of extensive strikes on Iran while Netanyahu presses Washington to join Israel in a four-to-seven-day air campaign; Trump has not decided.
key_facts.excerpt: US President Donald Trump is weighing another round of extensive military strikes against Iran as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu pushes Washington to join Israel in a four-to-seven-day air campaign, The New York Times reported Wednesday... Trump has not yet made a decision.

key_facts.fact: Israel has warned that Tehran has rebuilt missile and drone arsenals and advanced chemical and biological weapons programs; talks intensified when Mossad chief Roman Gofman met CIA Director John Ratcliffe in Washington last week.
key_facts.excerpt: He is weighing Israeli assessments that Iran is rebuilding its missile and drone capabilities and advancing efforts to develop chemical and biological weapons... Discussions intensified last week when Mossad chief Roman Gofman met with US officials in Washington, including CIA Director John Ratcliffe.

key_facts.fact: Administration officials are divided over the intelligence; the Times also reported Trump told VP JD Vance to abandon efforts to reach a negotiated settlement, favoring sustained economic pressure.
key_facts.excerpt: The newspaper also reported that Trump recently instructed Vice President JD Vance to abandon efforts to reach a negotiated settlement with Tehran, while increasingly favoring sustained economic pressure.

key_facts.fact: Trump told Fox News there are indications Iran 'is looking at gases, looking at bio' and that 'one way or the other, we'll finish it off'.
key_facts.excerpt: "Well, there is indication that Iran is looking at gases, looking at bio because we've shut them out with the nuclear," Trump told... "Yeah, I'm going to finish it off. Yeah, soon. I mean, one way or the other, we'll finish it off."

key_facts.fact: Officials from Gulf states, Pakistan and Turkey have stepped up calls with senior US officials to avert a resumption of all-out war, according to four regional officials cited by AP.
key_facts.excerpt: Government and security officials from the Persian Gulf countries, as well as Pakistan and Turkey, have engaged in concerted diplomacy, including phone calls with senior U.S. officials, in a bid to avert renewed war in the region.

key_facts.fact: On Wednesday the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two Houthi cruise missiles aimed at the Riyadh region, and a resident reported an 'extremely loud' explosion in the north of the Saudi capital.
key_facts.excerpt: On Wednesday, an "extremely loud" explosion was heard in the north of the Saudi capital Riyadh... The Saudi coalition said two Houthi cruise missiles targeting the Riyadh region were intercepted in separate incidents on Wednesday.

stories.headline: Fed minutes: nearly all officials see more hikes, and flag opaque AI debt as a financial-stability risk

key_facts.fact: Minutes of the Fed's Oct. 27-28 meeting, released Wednesday, show 'almost all participants' judged further rate increases would likely be appropriate; the FOMC held at 3.75%-4% in a 10-2 vote, with Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissenting for a quarter-point hike.
key_facts.excerpt: "almost all participants judged that... further action to raise the target range for the federal funds rate … would likely be appropriate"... the FOMC voted 10-2 to keep its benchmark overnight borrowing rate locked in a range between 3.75%-4%. Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented.

key_facts.fact: Fed staff warned that off-balance-sheet leasing commitments and circular financing among AI-related firms could amplify losses if AI returns disappoint; most participants said AI-related debt had grown rapidly through 'complex and opaque financing structures'.
key_facts.excerpt: "off-balance-sheet leasing commitments and circular financing arrangements among AI-related firms could amplify losses if returns on AI investment were to disappoint." "Most participants observed that AI-related debt had grown rapidly and that much of this growth had taken place through complex and opaque financing structures."

key_facts.fact: Policymakers called AI-linked demand 'a material source of inflation risk'; a couple said a move larger than a quarter point could be warranted in December.
key_facts.excerpt: Policymakers put artificial intelligence at the core of their discussions, indicating that demand associated with the technology would be "a material source of inflation risk."... A couple of participants even noted the possibility that a larger increase might be needed at the next policy meeting in December.

key_facts.fact: The Dow fell 561 points (-1.11%) to 50,198.17 and the S&P 500 posted its fifth straight decline; the 2-year Treasury yield rose to 4.804% while WTI crude fell 3.2% to $83.26 on a surprise inventory build.
key_facts.excerpt: Dow industrial average −561.25 points (−1.11%) to 50,198.17... 2-year yield 4.804% (+1.5 basis points)... December WTI settled at $83.26, down 3.20%

key_facts.fact: The dollar hit a 19-month high, gold fell 3% to a 14-month low of about $3,735/oz, and Brazil's real neared 6 per dollar.
key_facts.excerpt: Dollar +0.3% to fresh 19-month high, euro below $1.10... Brazil real nearing 6/$... Gold -3% to 14-month low of $3,735/oz.

stories.headline: US indicts alleged Russian agent who crossed from Mexico to spy on Palantir staff over Ukraine aid

key_facts.fact: A federal grand jury indicted Russian national Igor D'iu on charges of conspiring to act and acting as an unregistered agent of a foreign government, interstate stalking and ID fraud, targeting employees of a Silicon Valley technology and defense company, the DOJ said Wednesday, Nov. 18.
key_facts.excerpt: A federal grand jury has indicted Igor D'iu, a Russian national, on charges of conspiring to act as an agent of a foreign government, acting as an agent of a foreign government without notice to the Attorney General, interstate stalking, and fraud in connection with identification documents

key_facts.fact: Three people familiar with the investigation told NBC News the target was Palantir; the company is not named in the indictment.
key_facts.excerpt: The company is not named in the indictment. Three people familiar with the investigation told NBC News it was Palantir, which builds tools used by private companies and the Pentagon.

key_facts.fact: Recruited via Telegram and told he worked for 'the Motherland', D'iu flew from Istanbul to Mexico City in June 2026 and crossed the border illegally; he photographed employees' laptop screens at a coffee shop near the Palo Alto office and on Sept. 3 followed a female employee for nearly 30 miles.
key_facts.excerpt: D'iu traveled from Istanbul, Turkey, to Mexico City, Mexico, in June 2026, where his co-conspirators connected him with an individual who helped him cross the United States and Mexico border... On or about Sept. 3, D'iu allegedly followed a female employee... for nearly 30 miles

key_facts.fact: FBI searches recovered about $18,000 in cash, two Russian passports, an altered US passport under the name 'Hugo Landry Johns', and a notebook with employees' home addresses and profiles of at least three staff.
key_facts.excerpt: recovering approximately $18,000 in cash, two laptops, two iPhones, two Russian passports... a notebook containing 10 handwritten addresses... and detailed profiles of at least three employees

key_facts.fact: An industry source told the BBC it was the first time a Russian operative was found on US soil attempting to spy on the company, and that its systems were not penetrated.
key_facts.excerpt: the operation did not penetrate the company's private systems... this was the first time a Russian operative was found while on US soil attempting to spy on the company.

stories.headline: South Korea becomes fourth country to pass $1 trillion in annual exports, riding the AI chip boom

key_facts.fact: South Korea's cumulative 2026 exports passed $1 trillion at 2:09:38 p.m. local time on November 19, making it the fourth country after Germany, the US (both 2006) and China (2007) to reach the mark.
key_facts.excerpt: 대한민국 수출이 2026년 11월 19일 14시 09분 38초에 1조 달러를 달성했습니다... 기존 1조 달러 달성 국가(독일·미국 2006년, 중국 2007년)

key_facts.fact: Exports jumped from a record $709.3 billion in 2025; the government projects about $1.17 trillion for full-year 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The government projects annual exports will reach approximately $1.17 trillion this year, following last year's record of $709.3 billion.

key_facts.fact: Semiconductor exports reached $396.8 billion in January-October, nearly triple the $135.4 billion a year earlier, and account for 42.7% of total exports.
key_facts.excerpt: Semiconductors have driven this year's record, with exports surging 193-point-one percent year-on-year to 396-point-eight billion dollars in the January-October period, accounting for 42-point-seven percent of the total

key_facts.fact: The milestone puts South Korea ahead of Japan, whose exports peaked at $822.6 billion in 2011.
key_facts.excerpt: puts it ahead of Japan, whose exports peaked at 822-point-six billion dollars in 2011.

key_facts.fact: Officials warned that chip-price volatility, US and EU protectionism and Chinese oversupply could weigh on exports next year, and that the chip-led surge creates relatively few jobs.
key_facts.excerpt: The government said fluctuations in semiconductor prices, increased protectionism in the United States and the European Union (EU), and intensifying competition due to global oversupply could affect exports next year... The semiconductor sector has limited effects on job creation

stories.headline: UnitedHealth falls 10% and Humana 13% as CMS plans Medicare Advantage audit clawbacks back to 2018

key_facts.fact: On Wednesday UnitedHealth fell 10.2%, Humana 13.0%, Elevance 7.6%, CVS 5.2% and Cigna 3.0%, a second day of losses for health insurers.
key_facts.excerpt: Humana (HUM) -13.0% | UnitedHealth Group -10.2% | Elevance Health (ELV) -7.6% | CVS Health (CVS) -5.2% | The Cigna Group (CI) -3.0%

key_facts.fact: The trigger is CMS's proposed CRUSH anti-fraud rule, which would extrapolate Medicare Advantage audit findings to plans' wider payments starting with payment year 2018, recovering about $9 billion per payment year; CMS says the full rule could save nearly $90 billion over 10 years.
key_facts.excerpt: CMS would extrapolate what those audits find to a plan's wider payments, starting with audits of 2018. It estimates this would recover about $9B in overpayments for each payment year.

key_facts.fact: UnitedHealth's 10% loss dragged the Dow, where it carries a 4.32% weighting, to a session low; it pared UnitedHealth's year-to-date gain to 4%.
key_facts.excerpt: After Wednesday's 10% loss, shares of the largest health insurer by enrollees had pared their gains for the year to date to 4%.

key_facts.fact: Oppenheimer analysts expect the rule to face the same legal challenges that sank a comparable framework in court in 2025, and expect plans to price the cost into future bids; public comment runs to Jan. 19, 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: "We believe CMS will be subject to the same legal challenges that it faced in 2025," the analysts wrote... The proposal is open to public comment until Jan. 19, 2027.

key_facts.fact: Sen. Elizabeth Warren separately called for breaking up UnitedHealth, CVS and Cigna, citing the Break Up Big Medicine Act.
key_facts.excerpt: Senator Elizabeth Warren publicly called for breaking up vertically integrated healthcare conglomerates, specifically naming UnitedHealth alongside CVS and Cigna, and citing the Break Up Big Medicine Act

stories.headline: FDA approves Sanofi's Infilbray, first drug for the neurological symptoms of type 3 Gaucher disease

key_facts.fact: The FDA on November 18 approved Sanofi's venglustat (Infilbray) tablets as the first treatment for the neurological symptoms of type 3 Gaucher disease (GD3), for adults and children weighing at least 15 kg.
key_facts.excerpt: The FDA approved venglustat (Infilbray; Sanofi) tablets as the first treatment for the neurological symptoms of type 3 Gaucher disease (GD3) in adults and pediatric patients who weigh at least 15 kg (about 33 lb), according to an FDA news release issued November 18, 2026.

key_facts.fact: Infilbray is a once-daily oral glucosylceramide synthase inhibitor that crosses the blood-brain barrier; GD3 is a rare lysosomal storage disorder with central nervous system involvement.
key_facts.excerpt: Infilbray is a once-daily oral medicine that acts across the blood-brain barrier... GD3 is a rare lysosomal storage disorder that causes progressive systemic and neurologic decline, with central nervous system (CNS) manifestations.

key_facts.fact: In the 43-patient Phase 3 LEAP2MONO trial, Infilbray beat intravenous enzyme replacement therapy (imiglucerase) on a combined test of ataxia and cognition endpoints at 52 weeks (p=0.0137).
key_facts.excerpt: Infilbray demonstrated improvements in neurological manifestations over the enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) imiglucerase, with a global test of multiple neurological endpoints showing statistically significant superiority (p=0.0137).

key_facts.fact: The label carries warnings for suicidal ideation and behavior, lens opacification in children and embryo-fetal toxicity.
key_facts.excerpt: Infilbray carries Warnings and Precautions for Suicidal Ideation and Behavior, Lens Opacification in Pediatric Patients, and Embryofoetal Toxicity.
